newsitem.title: UK: IPE April gas oil ends slightly off ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE April gas oil ends slightly off ahead of expiry.

text.p: IPE April gas oil futures closed 25 cents down on Wednesday at $162.50 per tonne after good paper selling in the contract which expires on Thursday, brokers said.

"Obviously the market closed on the low side. We had a bounce an hour or so before the close back up to $163.50. Heating oil once again ticked off and we got a quite a lot of good paper selling in (April) gas oil," one broker said. "Gas oil has actually given up a little bit against the heating oil," he added. April gas oil closed $2.00 off the day's high of $164.50. May gas oil, which hit a high of $166 in earlier trade, closed up 25 cents at $164.25. "I would not be surprised if May (gas oil) has a correction after the expiry (of the April) contract, one or two days after the expiry, and go down towards the April trading levels," a trader said. May Brent was up 17 cents at $18.10 a barrel at 1703 GMT after bigger gains in earlier trade. The contract briefly touched a high of $18.34 shortly after NYMEX opened. Traders said the next resistance level for Brent was $18.36 with a big chart gap between $18.40 and $18.50. Brent was supported by technical factors and the gains made by the contract following the release late Tuesday of modestly bullish weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory data, traders said.
